title: Short hierarchically hyperbolic groups II: quotients and the Hopf property: the broad case of two odd components
author: Giorgio Mangioni, Alessandro Sisto
work: Short hierarchically hyperbolic groups II: quotients and the Hopf property
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Proposition (source0.tex lines 2022--2024, source label prop:2_odd_broad): if a large Artin group of hyperbolic type has a connected defining graph on at least three vertices with exactly two odd components, both of them broad, then the group is Hopfian; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 2026--2053 (one adjacent proof environment of 28 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span together with its retained context. Given a self-epimorphism and a nontrivial kernel element, it names the two odd components and analyses the image of one of them in three exhaustive cases: when that image is a central extension of a non-elementary hyperbolic group, when it is virtually free abelian of rank two but not contained in an edge group, and when it is a finite-index subgroup of an edge group; in each case it uses the peripheral structure of the group, the centraliser of the element joining the two odd components, the possible images of centralisers and dihedrals, and the rank of the abelianised image to produce a proper quotient that violates surjectivity, concluding that no nontrivial kernel element exists. The proposition is one of the two case analyses completing the article's main theorem that large Artin groups of hyperbolic type are Hopfian, and its statement and proof are research-level geometric group theory. H2: a research-level geometric-group-theory proposition whose proof combines the peripheral structure of Artin groups, centraliser and dihedral restrictions, hyperbolic-group theory and abelianisation-rank arguments in an exhaustive case analysis; it is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
